items.actClause:
AN ACT to amend the insurance law, in relation to enacting the "patient Rx
information and choice expansion act"
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S4620

SPONSOR: BRESLIN
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the insurance law, in relation to enacting the "patient
Rx information and choice expansion act"

 
PURPOSE:

The bill requires that real-time, patient specific, prescription drug
out-of-pocket cost details be provided at the point of prescribing which
will enable all patients a better understanding of what the out-of-
pocketò costs will be for their medications and greater transparency
overall.

 
SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section 1 titles the bill, the patient Rx information and choice expan-
sion act or the "PRICE" act.

Section 2 provides the definitions for terms related to patient
prescription pricing transparency. The section also establishes an inte-
gration requirement for health plans to allow real time benefit informa-
tion to be available immediately. The information that is required to be
provided in the real time benefit tool is outlined which includes
prescription cost and benefit information, cost sharing, eligibility,
alternatives, and prior authorization.

Section 3 sets the effective date.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

This bill seeks to address affordability and transparency issues that
affect prescription drug use and adherence. The out-of-pocket cost
burden for medically necessary treatments for patients can negatively
impact the likelihood of beginning treatment and adherence, leading to
overall drug abandonment rates. In addition, the use of high deductible
plans is growing resulting in increased costs for patients for medically
necessary treatments.

Patient nonadherence to necessary prescribed medications is associated
with poor clinical outcomes, progression of disease, and an estimated
burden of billions per year in avoidable direct health care costs.
Between $100 and $300 billion of avoidable health care costs have been
attributed to nonadherence in the U.S. annually, representing 3 to 10%
of total US health care costs. The Centers for Medicare and Medicaid
Services (CMS) have found that health plans and entities acting on their
behalf may have misaligned incentives driving utilization of higher cost
medicines and hindering patient choice to lower cost options due to a
lack of price transparency. Per CMS, prescription price transparency is
critical to lowering overall drug costs and patient out-of-pocket costs
and supports improved medication adherence. At a time when patients are
being required to pay more and more out-of-pocket for healthcare, they
need access to real-time, patient-specific information via means of
their choosing.  To achieve cost savings, patients must understand their
drug benefit coverage and payment considerations for drugs on and off a
plan's formulary, including lower cost clinical and therapeutic alterna-
tives.  The real time benefit tool provides a proactive look at which
medications need prior approval. The tool will allow an alternative
prescription or will alert the provider that a prior approval is needed
and a process to expedite the steps to acquire a prior approval.

Due to the COVID-19 pandemic, healthcare professionals may not always be
available to assist patients as they navigate prescription cost process
and now, more than ever, patients need access to tools and resources at
all points in the prescription process that empowers them with them
up-to-date prescription pricing options.

 
LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

New bill

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act shall take effect July 1, 2023.

approvalMessage.text:
APPROVAL MEMORANDUM - No. 104 Chapter 826
 
       MEMORANDUM filed with Senate Bill Number 4620-C, entitled:
 
    "AN  ACT  to  amend  the  insurance law, in relation to enacting the
        'patient Rx information and choice expansion act'"
 
    APPROVED
 
  This bill would require health plans to furnish their  cost,  benefit,
and  coverage  data  to  the enrollee, their health care provider, or an
authorized third party upon request. Such information would be  provided
in  real time to enable patients to better understand coverage, co-pays,
and their out-of-pocket expenses and to protect them from  surprises  at
the pharmacy counter.
 
  I support increasing communication to New Yorkers to help ensure well-
informed health care decisions. This legislation would require what many
managed  care  companies  already  do under existing practice, providing
patients with their coverage information  in  real  time  through  smart
phone  applications  or online access. Therefore, systems and technology
are already in place to implement this requirement. I reached an  agree-
ment with the Legislature on some technical changes to effectively inte-
grate this requirement into the Insurance Law.
 
  On  the  basis  of this agreement, I am pleased to sign this bill into
law.
 
  This bill is approved.                           (signed) KATHY HOCHUL
 
                                 ______

summary: Requires health plans operating in the state to furnish the cost, benefit, and coverage data as required to the enrollee, his or her health care provider, or the third-party of his or her choosing.
title: Enacts the "patient Rx information and choice expansion act"
